claims.text: Treating a Pulumi Output<T> as a plain value (e.g., calling toString on it) produces placeholder text such as `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` in log lines, generated files, or resource properties.
A page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ titled 'Output value errors' that covers this and other symptoms of treating an output as if it were already a plain value.
The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ exists and covers errors from stringifying, branching on, or reading a Pulumi output value as if it were a plain value.
Pulumi Cloud/CLI returns the error "409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress" when an update conflicts with an in-progress update.
Pulumi Cloud can return 500 internal server errors.
When the Pulumi CLI cannot access a self-managed (DIY) state backend, it produces a `read ".pulumi/meta.yaml"` error.
The page /docs/iac/operations/stack-management/using-a-diy-backend/ has an anchor #error-reading-pulumimetayaml.
Crashes or hangs on Apple Silicon can be caused by x86_64 binaries running under Rosetta 2.
A recently deleted stack can be recovered from the Pulumi Cloud console, including after an accidental `pulumi stack rm --force`.
Pulumi supports `--target` and `--exclude` flags to limit operations to specific resources.
Running `pulumi logs share` securely sends the logs from a failed operation to the Pulumi team.
The logging guide at /docs/iac/operations/debugging/logging/ has an #automatic-logging section.
The logging guide has a #cli-verbose-logging section.
Pulumi dev builds are pre-release builds that provide bug fixes not yet shipped in a stable release.
Pulumi offers paid support options.
Pulumi resource properties are represented as Outputs rather than plain values because their real values are not known until the resource has been created or updated.

Converting a Pulumi Output to a string directly (instead of via apply or an equivalent helper) does not raise an error by default; Pulumi silently substitutes a placeholder message in place of the value.

In the TypeScript SDK, the string conversion of an Output contains the literal text `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `apply` or `pulumi.interpolate`.
In the TypeScript SDK, calling `JSON.stringify()` on an Output produces a `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` string rather than the value.
In the Python SDK, formatting an Output as a string yields text containing `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported`, and Pulumi also logs a warning.
In Python, passing an Output to `json.dumps()` fails with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`; `Output.json_dumps()` is the alternative.
Python's Pulumi SDK provides `Output.json_dumps()`, `Output.concat` and `Output.format`.
In Go, passing a `pulumi.StringOutput` where a `string` is expected is a compile error, and values are resolved inside `ApplyT`.
In the C# SDK, the string conversion of an Output contains the literal text `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `Apply` or `Output.Format`.

Setting the environment variable `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true` (supported in TypeScript, Python, and C#) makes converting an Output to a string throw an exception instead of returning the placeholder text.
`pulumi.interpolate` and `pulumi.concat` are the TypeScript string-composition helpers for Outputs; `pulumi.Sprintf` and `pulumi.JSONMarshal` are the Go helpers; `Output.Format` is the C# helper.

An `apply` callback runs asynchronously once the output resolves, generally after the program's top-level code has finished running, so an outer variable assigned inside it is still undefined when read at top level.
Most resource inputs accept Outputs as well as plain values, while a handful of positions such as a resource's logical name cannot.

In dynamically typed languages an `if` on an Output evaluates the Output object itself and is generally always true; in statically typed languages it is usually a compile error because `Output<bool>` is not a `bool`.
Values known at program start, such as stack configuration read with `pulumi.Config`, environment variables, or hardcoded flags, are plain values that can be branched on normally.
Passing an Output as a resource logical name, loop bound or map key fails to compile in TypeScript, Go, and C#.
In Python, passing an Output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string`.
In Python, using an Output as a loop bound (`range(some_output)`) raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.
In Python, using an Output as a dictionary key does not raise; it silently keys on the Output object itself.
A StackReference lets a separate stack consume another stack's outputs.
Pulumi has no supported way to block the program and synchronously read a resolved value from an Output.
`pulumi stack output <name>` reads a single stack output from the CLI after a deployment.
The Automation API exposes an `outputs` field on the result of running an update (e.g. `res.Outputs` in Go).
Linked docs pages exist: /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/apply/, /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/all/, /docs/iac/concepts/stacks/#stackreferences, /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/.
